title: System Design: Scalable URL Shortener (TinyURL / Bitly)

evaluationCriteria: Deep understanding of HTTP Redirection (301 vs 302)
Resilient error handling, monitoring, and legal compliance

functionalRequirements: Shortening: Convert any long URL into a unique, compact short URL.
Redirection: Forward visitors from the short URL to the original long URL with minimal latency.
Custom Short Links (Vanity URLs): Allow users to define custom aliases (e.g., tiny.url/my-portfolio).
Expiration: Support an optional or default expiration date (e.g., 1 year of inactivity).
Analytics: Track engagement metrics (total clicks, referrers, device types, geolocations).
User Accounts: Enable user authentication to manage, edit, and delete their shortened links.
nonFunctionalRequirements: High Availability: 99.99% uptime. The redirection service must remain accessible even if write servers lag.
Ultra-Low Latency: Real-time redirection with sub-10ms cache hits and sub-50ms database hits.
Strict Uniqueness: No two distinct long URLs may receive the same short alias unless explicitly intended.
Non-Predictable: Short URLs should be random and non-sequential to prevent scrapers from enumerating private URLs.
Scalability: Read-heavy system handling thousands of read requests per second smoothly.

assumptions.averageURLSize: 90 bytes (Average Long URL size) + ~410 bytes metadata = ~500 bytes per record

storageEstimations.dailyStorage: 80 Million * 90 bytes = 7.2 GB/day (Raw URL) -> ~40 GB/day with indexes and metadata

memoryAndCaching.paretoPrinciple: 80-20 Rule: 20% of hot URLs generate 80% of read traffic.
memoryAndCaching.verdict: A standard multi-node Redis cluster with 64 GB to 128 GB memory easily holds all hot links in RAM using an LRU eviction policy.

base62Encoding.definition: A 62-character alphanumeric set consisting of [0-9] (10 digits), [a-z] (26 lowercase), and [A-Z] (26 uppercase).
base62Encoding.whyNotBase64: Base-64 introduces reserved URL characters like '+' and '/' which require percent-encoding (%2B, %2F) in query parameters.

lengthCapacityMath.length7: 62^7 = ~3.52 Trillion unique URLs (Easily exceeds our 146 Billion requirement for 5+ years)

md5Approach.howItWorks: Hash the long URL using MD5 (128-bit hex digest) and take the first 6-7 characters.
md5Approach.fatalFlaw: Hash Collisions! Different long URLs can yield identical 7-character prefixes. Resolving collisions requires database lookups, salting, and rehashing in loops, introducing unpredictable latency.

counterBasedBase62Approach.howItWorks: Generate a globally unique 64-bit integer ID first, then convert that integer directly into Base-62.
counterBasedBase62Approach.advantage: 100% collision-free. Every unique integer maps to a unique Base-62 string with zero database collision retries.

zookeeperRangeAllocation.purpose: Coordinates distributed unique integer range allocations across application servers without single points of failure.
howItWorks: ZooKeeper maintains a global atomic counter in its ephemeral znode structure.
When App Server 1 boots up, it requests a range from ZooKeeper. ZooKeeper assigns [1,000,000 to 2,000,000].
When App Server 2 boots up, ZooKeeper assigns [2,000,001 to 3,000,000].
Each application server increments its local atomic counter in memory without making network calls.
When an app server exhausts its range, it queries ZooKeeper for the next unused range chunk (e.g., [3,000,001 to 4,000,000]).
zookeeperRangeAllocation.faultTolerance: If an app server crashes, only its remaining unallocated local range numbers are skipped, which is totally acceptable in a 3.5-trillion-capacity namespace.

http301_PermanentRedirect.behavior: Browsers cache the redirection locally. Subsequent clicks go straight from browser cache to destination.
http301_PermanentRedirect.tradeOff: Saves server load, BUT completely bypasses backend servers, making analytics and click tracking impossible.

http302_TemporaryRedirect.behavior: Browsers always contact the URL shortener service on every click before redirecting.
http302_TemporaryRedirect.tradeOff: Slightly higher server traffic, BUT enables 100% accurate click analytics, bot inspection, and instant link revocation.
http302_TemporaryRedirect.verdict: Use HTTP 302 Found (or 307 Temporary Redirect) for tracking and monetization platforms.

step4_dataModelAndDatabaseDesign.databaseChoice: NoSQL Distributed Key-Value / Wide-Column Store (Cassandra, DynamoDB, or MongoDB)
justification: Access patterns are simple Key-Value lookups (no relational multi-table JOINs required).
Massive horizontal scaling across shards with multi-master replication.
Partition Key is `short_url_text`, providing O(1) single-partition lookups at multi-terabyte scale.

components: Clients: Mobile apps and Web browsers.
DNS / Anycast CDN: Terminates SSL and routes traffic to the nearest regional Point of Presence.
Load Balancer: Nginx / AWS ALB using Consistent Hashing to distribute load to healthy App Servers.
Application Servers: Stateless Flask / Go / Java services executing Base-62 conversions and redirect logic.
ZooKeeper Cluster: Manages distributed numeric ID sequence ranges.
Redis Cache: In-memory LRU cache storing the top 20% most active URLs.
Persistent Database: NoSQL cluster (Cassandra / DynamoDB) storing mapping data.
Async Analytics Pipeline: Kafka message queue + Spark/Flink consumers flushing metrics to ClickHouse / Snowflake.
writeFlow: 1. User sends POST /shorten request with the long URL (and optional custom alias / expiry).
2. Load balancer forwards request to an available application server.
3. If a custom alias is provided, the server verifies whether the alias is available and not a reserved keyword (e.g., 'admin', 'login').
4. If no custom alias is provided, the server fetches the next local sequential integer from its allocated ZooKeeper range.
5. The integer is encoded into a 7-character Base-62 short code.
6. The mapping is persisted to the database and pre-warmed in Redis cache.
7. The short URL is returned to the user.
readFlow: 2. Request hits the Load Balancer and is assigned to an App Server.
3. App Server checks Redis Cache: On Cache Hit -> immediately sends HTTP 302 redirect with Location header.
4. On Cache Miss -> Server queries Database. If found, sets key in Redis with LRU policy and sends HTTP 302 redirect.
5. If link is expired or does not exist, returns HTTP 404.
6. Concurrently, an asynchronous telemetry event is emitted to Apache Kafka for analytics processing without slowing down user redirect.

linkExpirationHandling.problem: Running periodic batch scripts like `DELETE FROM urls WHERE expires_at < NOW()` locks tables and triggers heavy disk IOPS.
linkExpirationHandling.solution: Combine two patterns: (1) Lazy / Passive Expiration on read (if current timestamp > expiry timestamp, return 404 and evict from cache); (2) Native Database TTL policies (Redis EXPIRE and DynamoDB TTL daemons clean up cold dead records in the background without affecting app servers).

securityAndAbusePrevention.rateLimiting: Enforce Token Bucket or Sliding Window rate limiting per IP / API token at the API Gateway level (e.g., 50 req/min for free users) to prevent automated link-generation spam.
securityAndAbusePrevention.malwareAndPhishingDefense: Integrate Google Safe Browsing API or a Bloom filter blacklist on the write path to intercept known malicious domains before generating short aliases.

loggingMonitoringAndAlerting.telemetry: Export P99 read/write latency, Cache Hit Ratio, and 4xx/5xx HTTP error rate metrics into Prometheus and visualize via Grafana.
loggingMonitoringAndAlerting.alerting: Trigger automated PagerDuty / SMTP alerts if Redis cache hit ratio drops below 70% or 5xx server errors exceed 1% over a 5-minute rolling window.
